evidence:
The frozen XLSX was opened with openpyxl, including Quality Checks row 47 (number 46), Internal Quality Checks row 47, and the relevant deterministic Dockerfile/secret/isolation descriptions. The internal row repeats that the agent cannot read criteria or influence reward; it adds no alternate profile. Independently SHA256-checked all 50 frozen task files and all 34 frozen rule files against manifest.json: zero mismatches.

Source inspection supports the intended isolation, with no demonstrated source defect. All task-relative paths below are within .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task. environment/Dockerfile:9-15 installs only express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 and copies only instructions/ and assets/; lines 17-23 create an otherwise empty /app with .gitkeep. I read every copied note and the complete seed. No criteria, grader client, RewardKit, answer implementation, rubric or key is included. The tree contains no symlinks. An exact-token comparison of all 79 criterion IDs parsed from all five judge.toml files against instruction.md and every environment file found zero matches. This complements the manual public-content inspection rather than replacing it. task.toml:2 exports only /app and /assets, :28 explicitly says environment_mode = "separate", and :30-35 confines the templated provider credential to verifier.env.

The verifier owns its tests and reward. tests/Dockerfile:17-19 installs the judge/browser clients and :31 installs harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7 only there; :43-44 says COPY . /tests and chmod -R go-rwx /tests. tests/test.sh:3 uses umask 077, :10-12 makes the log directory mode 700 and reapplies /tests restrictions. Lines 72-83 reject symlinks outside the declared /app/node_modules boundary. Lines 104-111 start the submission with env -i, a five-variable application environment and setpriv --reuid=65534 --regid=65534 --clear-groups; lines 160-167 repeat the sanitized unprivileged launch on restart. The application receives neither ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN nor REWARDKIT_* through that environment. tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:34-40 gives its subprocess only PATH. tests/tools/score.py:10 resolves the policy from the protected /tests tree; :59-60 writes the final reward into the protected log directory.

Adversarial source checks: a conforming implementation with ordinary /app files, an alternative frontend, and internal node_modules symlinks does not need /tests or grading credentials, and this separation imposes no extra frontend requirement. A malicious server that tries to read /tests/scored/functional/judge.toml, overwrite /logs/verifier/reward.json, or obtain the provider key from its own environment is opposed by the explicit UID/mode/environment boundaries above. No credible false pass or false fail was established. These are source-level checks; no permission probe was executed.

The missing measurement is actual final-image isolation, not a discovered leak. The raw-evidence-index explicitly limits supplied evidence to scripted browser observations and says no full verifier run was supplied. Its RESULTS.json hash was independently verified as ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09. Its isolation observations concern the product's browser snippet sandbox, not build-container contents or an application UID reading grading files/key/reward output. No final-image inventory or permission-denial probe is available in the indexed evidence. New Docker runs are forbidden by this review prompt. Thus source boundaries look correct, but the row's actual-image claim remains unexercised; this report does not certify runtime isolation or a configured judge/Oracle pass.
suggested_fix: No source correction is established. Before runtime clearance, inspect the exact built agent image for grading material and use a harmless unprivileged verifier probe to record denied reads of criteria and provider credentials and denied writes to reward outputs; bind those observations to these frozen hashes.
